mainTopic: The water of the כיור, the source that a ערל כהן disqualifies the עבודה, and the זקני דרום's view that a טמא מת כהן can bring acceptance
overview: This amud first finishes a discussion about the water of the כיור. The גמרא tries to prove it must be מים חיים, then answers that this is a dispute between תנאים: רבי ישמעאל requires spring water, and the חכמים allow any water. Next the גמרא asks for the source that a ערל כהן disqualifies the עבודה. רב חסדא says it comes from פסוקים in יחזקאל, not from the תורה of משה. A ברייתא explains that the פסוק includes both a ערל לב and a ערל בשר, and the גמרא shows why both had to be written. Then the גמרא turns to a טמא כהן. The זקני דרום say only a טמא שרץ disqualifies, while a טמא מת כהן's service is accepted. Through a series of challenges, including a קל וחומר from ריש לקיש, the גמרא clarifies their views about the פסח of a טמא owner. A new challenge from a פסוק begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof that Basin water must be flowing water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the earlier source cannot mean actual כיור water, so it must mean water fit for the כיור. That shows כיור water is a special kind: מים חיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Would you say the source excludes actual Basin water, which already has its own special name? Rather, it must mean water fit to be Basin water. So Basin water must be flowing water!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a line of reasoning that tries to prove that the water of the כיור must be flowing water (מים חיים).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Actual כיור water is called by a special name ('water of the כיור'), so the plain word 'water' would not include it anyway. That means the source must be talking about a kind of water that is defined by being fit for the כיור. The only thing that would make water a special category like that is being flowing water.

keyTerms.meaning: The Basin in the מקדש that the כהנים washed from
A modifier name, a name with an extra description attached
Rather, is it not... (introduces the only reading left)
Apparently, so we see
Flowing water, like spring water

phrases.english: Would you say excluded is the water of the Basin,
which has a modifier in its name?
phrases.notes: It's not just called 'water' but 'water of the כיור', so plain 'water' wouldn't include it to begin with.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not
water that is fit to be water of the Basin?
Apparently, it is flowing water!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו דִּרְאוּיִין לְמֵי כִיּוֹר? אַלְמָא מַיִם חַיִּים נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an argument begun before this section about what kind of water the כיור needs.
steps.raayaObject: That the water of the כיור must be מים חיים
steps.raayaSupportSource: An earlier source that excluded 'water of the כיור', which can only mean water fit for the כיור

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the proof only works for one opinion: רבי ישמעאל requires spring water for the כיור, while the חכמים allow other water.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a dispute between תנאים. רבי יוחנן said: about the Basin water, רבי ישמעאל says it must be spring water, and the חכמים say it can be other water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the proof by saying that the question of כיור water is an argument between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from Step 1 is true, but only according to רבי ישמעאל, who requires spring water. The חכמים disagree and allow any water, so the source does not settle the question for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
Spring water
Other water, any kind of water

steps.whatToRemember: Whether כיור water must be מים חיים is a dispute: רבי ישמעאל says spring water, the חכמים say any water.

phrases.english: It is a dispute between Tannaim.
As Rabbi Yochanan says:
The water of the Basin:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: מֵי מַעְיָן הֵן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says: it must be spring water,
and the Rabbis say: it may be other water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof of Step 1 by showing it reflects only one side of a dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A dispute between תנאים: the proof holds only for one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source proves that everyone requires מים חיים for the כיור
steps.terutzMaskana: Only רבי ישמעאל requires spring water; the חכמים allow other water

steps.title: Source for disqualifying an uncircumcised priest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה and asks for the source that a ערל disqualifies the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: An uncircumcised כהן: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic, asking where we learn that a ערל כהן disqualifies the עבודה. This sets up רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed people whose עבודה is invalid, including a ערל. The גמרא now wants the source for that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An uncircumcised man
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: An uncircumcised priest: from where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the כיור discussion and turns to a new case from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a ערל כהן may not do the עבודה

steps.title: רב חסדא: learned from יחזקאל, not from the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says this rule is not found in the תורה of משה but in the words of the נביא יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: We did not learn this from the תורה of משה רבינו. We learned it from the words of יחזקאל בן בוזי: 'No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart or uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter My Sanctuary to serve Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by quoting a פסוק from יחזקאל that says a ערל may not serve in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the גמרא looks for a source in the חומש. Here רב חסדא openly says the source is in נביאים. The פסוק shows a ערל may not serve, but it does not yet say his עבודה is invalid after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה of משה, our teacher (the חומש)
The נביא יחזקאל, son of בוזי
A foreigner, a stranger
Uncircumcised in heart

steps.confusionAlert: This is a famous case where a halacha is learned from a נביא and not from the חומש. רב חסדא himself points this out.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda says:
This matter, from the Torah of Moses our teacher,
we did not learn;
from the words of Ezekiel son of Buzi we learned it:
"No foreigner,
uncircumcised in heart or uncircumcised in flesh,
shall enter into My Sanctuary to serve Me."

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר זֶה מִתּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לֹא לָמַדְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is יחזקאל 44:9, which forbids a ערל from serving in the מקדש

steps.title: Source that he profanes the service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a further source: that a ערל's עבודה is actually profaned, meaning invalid after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that he profanes the עבודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question, setting up a second פסוק. The first פסוק said a ערל should not serve; now we need proof that if he did, the עבודה is ruined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being told not to do something is different from saying it does not count once done. The משנה says the עבודה is disqualified, so the גמרא needs a source for that stronger rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He profanes the עבודה, making it invalid

phrases.english: And from where do we derive that he desecrates the service?
phrases.notes: Even after the fact, the עבודה he did is invalid, not just that he shouldn't have done it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 4: that פסוק forbids serving, but does not show the עבודה is invalid.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a ערל's עבודה is invalid after the fact

steps.title: The verse says it profanes My house
steps.stepSummary: A second פסוק in יחזקאל says that bringing a ערל into the מקדש profanes it, showing his עבודה is profaned.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'When you brought in foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in My Sanctuary, to profane My house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with another פסוק from יחזקאל that uses the word 'profane' about a ערל in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לחלל, 'to profane', shows that a ערל's presence and service actually spoil the holy service. That is the source that his עבודה is invalid, not merely forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: To profane, to make unholy
As it is written

steps.whatToRemember: A ערל כהן is barred from the עבודה (יחזקאל 44:9) and his עבודה is invalid because the פסוק calls it profaning (יחזקאל 44:7). Both come from יחזקאל, not the חומש.

phrases.english: As it is written: "In that you have brought in foreigners,
uncircumcised in heart or uncircumcised in flesh,
to be in My Sanctuary,
to profane My house."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יחזקאל 44:7 says bringing a ערל into the מקדש is 'to profane My house', so his עבודה is profaned

steps.title: A ברייתא explains what 'בן נכר' means
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 'בן נכר' in the פסוק is not a real non-Jew, since the פסוק adds 'ערל לב'. It means a Jew whose actions are estranged from ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'A stranger.' Could it mean an actual stranger? The verse says 'uncircumcised in heart.' If so, why does it say 'stranger'? It means someone whose actions have become estranged from his Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the words 'בן נכר' in the פסוק from יחזקאל that was just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think 'בן נכר' means a non-Jew. But the פסוק goes on to say 'ערל לב', which describes the kind of person being disqualified. So 'בן נכר' must describe a Jew (a כהן) whose behavior has made him a stranger to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: A stranger, here meaning someone estranged from ה׳
Uncircumcised in heart, meaning someone whose heart is closed to ה׳
One might have thought
The verse teaches (to say otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: 'בן נכר' here does NOT mean a non-Jew. It describes a Jew whose actions are far from ה׳.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"A stranger": might it mean an actual stranger?
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 44:9. An 'actual stranger' means a non-Jew.

phrases.english: The verse says "uncircumcised in heart."

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״בֶּן נֵכָר״?
phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say "stranger"?
It means one whose actions have become estranged
from his Father in Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״בֶּן נֵכָר״ – יָכוֹל בֶּן נֵכָר מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words of the יחזקאל פסוק used as the source in steps 4 and 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בן נכר' in the פסוק refers to a Jew whose actions are estranged from ה׳, not a non-Jew.

steps.title: A ערל בשר is also disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the word 'ערל לב' alone would cover only that case, so the פסוק adds 'וערל בשר' to include a physically uncircumcised כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I only know about one uncircumcised in heart. From where do we know about one uncircumcised in flesh? The verse says 'and uncircumcised in flesh.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows that the same פסוק also disqualifies a כהן who is physically uncircumcised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the ברייתא has taught only about a ערל לב. The extra words 'וערל בשר' in the פסוק add a physically uncircumcised person, which is the ערל discussed in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Uncircumcised in flesh, meaning physically not circumcised
I only know (from this source) about
From where do we know?

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק disqualifies both a ערל לב (heart far from ה׳) and a ערל בשר (physically uncircumcised).

phrases.english: And I only have one uncircumcised in heart;
from where do we know one uncircumcised in flesh?
The verse says: "and uncircumcised in flesh."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא עֶרֶל לֵב; עֶרֶל בָּשָׂר מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, adding the second case from the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ערל בשר is also disqualified, learned from the words 'וערל בשר'.

steps.title: Why the פסוק needs both ערל לב and ערל בשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that each case has its own reason. You could not learn one from the other, so the פסוק needs to mention both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If the Torah had written only 'uncircumcised in flesh,' I would say it is because he is repulsive, but one uncircumcised in heart, who is not repulsive, is not disqualified. And if it had taught only 'uncircumcised in heart,' I would say it is because his heart is not toward Heaven, but one uncircumcised in flesh, whose heart is toward Heaven, is not disqualified. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the פסוק has to mention both kinds of ערל instead of just one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ערל בשר is disqualified because his body is repulsive, and that does not apply to a ערל לב. A ערל לב is disqualified because his heart is not toward ה׳, and that does not apply to a ערל בשר. Since the reasons differ, neither case teaches the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Both are needed
Repulsive or disgusting
The Merciful One (the Torah)
I would say not

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic צריכותא pattern. The גמרא shows that each phrase in a פסוק teaches something you could not have learned from the other.

phrases.english: And both are needed;
for if the Merciful One had written only "uncircumcised in flesh,"
that would be because he is repulsive;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עֶרֶל לֵב, דְּלָא מְאִיס – אֵימָא לָא.
phrases.english: but one uncircumcised in heart, who is not repulsive, I would say is not disqualified.
And if it had taught us only uncircumcised in heart,
that would be because his heart is not toward Heaven;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עֶרֶל בָּשָׂר, דְּלִבּוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם – אֵימָא לָא;
phrases.english: but one uncircumcised in flesh, whose heart is toward Heaven, I would say is not disqualified;
so both are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question of why the ברייתא needed both phrases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both ערל לב and ערל בשר must be written, since each has a separate reason for disqualification.

steps.title: The זקני דרום limit the rule of טמא to a טמא שרץ
steps.stepSummary: Moving to the next item in the משנה, the זקני דרום say a טמא disqualifies the עבודה only if he is a טמא שרץ. A טמא מת is different: since he can bring acceptance for the community, he can also do so for an individual.
steps.simpleTranslation: An impure person is disqualified. The Elders of the South said: They taught this only about one impure from a creeping animal. But one impure from a corpse, since he brings acceptance for the community, also brings acceptance for an individual.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, a טמא כהן, and brings a statement that narrows the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זקני דרום say the משנה's rule applies only to a טמא שרץ. A טמא מת may serve for the community when it is in טומאה, so after the fact his service for an individual's קרבן is also accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: The Elders of the South
Impure from touching a dead creeping animal
Impure from a dead body
Brings acceptance (makes the קרבן accepted)
Community / individual

steps.confusionAlert: The זקני דרום are not saying a טמא מת is pure. They are saying his service still works, as a special outcome for that kind of טומאה.

phrases.english: An impure one is disqualified.
The Elders of the South said:
They taught this only about one impure from a creeping animal;
but one impure from a corpse,
since he brings acceptance for the community,
phrases.notes: When most of the community is impure from a dead body, communal קרבנות are brought even in that state.

phrases.english: he also brings acceptance for an individual.

steps.triggerLanguage: טָמֵא פָּסוּל. אָמְרוּ זִקְנֵי דָרוֹם: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא טְמֵא שֶׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from ערל to the next item in the משנה, טמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a טמא שרץ disqualifies the עבודה. A טמא מת's service is accepted for an individual after the fact, since he can serve for the community.

steps.title: A קל וחומר challenge: a טמא שרץ should be even better
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the זקני דרום. A טמא מת has the more severe טומאה and needs sprinkling on the third and seventh days. If his service brings acceptance, a טמא שרץ, whose טומאה is lighter, should be able to bring acceptance too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let one impure from a creeping animal also be included by a קל וחומר from one impure from a corpse. If one impure from a corpse, who needs sprinkling on the third and seventh day, brings acceptance, then one impure from a creeping animal, who does not need that sprinkling, should surely bring acceptance!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the זקני דרום's distinction using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their rule makes the more severe טומאה (מת) work better than the lighter one (שרץ). That seems backwards. If the severe case is accepted, the lighter case should be accepted all the more, and then nothing would be left for the משנה's rule to disqualify.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
An argument from a stricter case to a lighter one
Sprinkling (of פרה אדומה water) on the third and seventh days
Isn't it logical?

phrases.english: If so, one impure from a creeping animal as well,
let it be learned by a קל וחומר from one impure from a corpse:
just as one impure from a corpse,
who needs sprinkling on the third and seventh day, brings acceptance;
one impure from a creeping animal,
who does not need sprinkling on the third and seventh day,
is it not logical that he brings acceptance?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, טְמֵא שֶׁרֶץ נָמֵי – לֵיתֵי בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר מִטְּמֵא מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges the distinction the זקני דרום made in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The זקני דרום's claim that a טמא מת brings acceptance but a טמא שרץ does not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: the lighter טומאה (שרץ, with no sprinkling needed) should be at least as acceptable as the heavier טומאה (מת, which needs sprinkling).

steps.title: The priests are compared to the people being atoned for
steps.stepSummary: The זקני דרום compare the כהנים (מכפרין) to the ציבור (מתכפרין). The ציבור's offering may be brought when they are טמא מת but not when they are טמא שרץ. The same is true for the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The זקני דרום hold that the ones who bring atonement are like the ones who receive atonement. With the ones receiving atonement, if they are טמא מת the offering is brought, but if they are טמא שרץ it is not. So too with the ones bringing atonement: a טמא מת כהן works, a טמא שרץ כהן does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 11, which asked why the lighter טמא שרץ should be worse than the heavier טמא מת. The זקני דרום are not using a קל וחומר. They are copying the rule of the ציבור onto the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not based on which טומאה is more severe. It follows a parallel: the ציבור may offer while טמא מת but not while טמא שרץ, and the כהנים follow the same pattern. That is why the 'lighter' טמא שרץ ends up disqualifying.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold / they are of the opinion
The Elders of the South
Those who bring atonement: the כהנים doing the service
Those who receive atonement: the owners of the קרבן, here the ציבור
Yes / no

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying טמא שרץ is a stronger טומאה. It isn't. The זקני דרום are simply matching the כהנים to the rule of the ציבור.

phrases.english: The Elders of the South hold:
those who bring atonement are like those who receive atonement;
phrases.notes: מכפרין are the כהנים doing the service. מתכפרין are the people the קרבן is for, here the ציבור.

phrases.english: just as with those who receive atonement, if they are impure from a corpse, yes [the offering is brought],
if they are impure from a creeping animal, no;
so too with those who bring atonement: if impure from a corpse, yes [their service works],
if impure from a creeping animal, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different basis for the rule: a parallel to the ציבור instead of a קל וחומר based on severity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A טמא מת כהן works, so the lighter טמא שרץ כהן should certainly work
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהנים follow the pattern of the ציבור: טמא מת yes, טמא שרץ no
steps.whyThisMatters: This parallel drives the rest of the discussion. The גמרא first checks what it assumes, and then ריש לקיש uses its results to attack the ruling that a טמא מת כהן brings acceptance.

steps.title: What do they hold about the פסח of a טמא שרץ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the זקני דרום hold about bringing the קרבן פסח for an owner who is טמא שרץ. If they say it is not brought, that runs into the rule that whatever pushes off an individual lets the ציבור bring its offering in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do they hold? If they hold that we do not slaughter the פסח and sprinkle its blood for someone who is טמא שרץ, then why can't the ציבור bring its offerings in that טומאה? There is a rule that any טומאה that pushes off an individual is a טומאה the ציבור may offer in!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the assumption from step 12 that the ציבור cannot offer while טמא שרץ. It asks which view on the פסח could fit that assumption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule: any טומאה that pushes an individual off to פסח שני is a טומאה the ציבור may offer in. So if a טמא שרץ individual is pushed off, the ציבור should be allowed to offer while טמא שרץ. That would break the parallel in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: We slaughter the animal and sprinkle its blood
Is pushed off, here to פסח שני
The community
In a state of impurity
Why?

phrases.english: What do they hold?
If they hold: we do not slaughter and sprinkle
phrases.notes: This is talking about the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: for someone impure from a creeping animal;
why can't the community perform [its offerings] in impurity?
But anything for which an individual is pushed off,
phrases.notes: Pushed off means he has to wait for פסח שני.

phrases.english: the community performs [its offerings] in impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the hidden assumption in step 12 that the ציבור cannot offer while טמא שרץ
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption in step 12 that the ציבור cannot offer while טמא שרץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a טמא שרץ individual is pushed off from the פסח, then the rule 'whatever pushes off an individual lets the ציבור offer in טומאה' would allow the ציבור to offer while טמא שרץ

steps.title: They must hold the פסח is brought for a טמא שרץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the זקני דרום hold the פסח is slaughtered and its blood sprinkled for an owner who is טמא שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they hold that we do slaughter and sprinkle for someone who is טמא שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question from step 13 by giving the זקני דרום the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The individual who is טמא שרץ is not pushed off, since the פסח is brought for him. So the rule from step 13 does not apply, and the ציבור has no permission to offer while טמא שרץ. The parallel from step 12 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather

phrases.english: Rather, they hold:
we slaughter and sprinkle for someone impure from a creeping animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא קָסָבְרִי: שׁוֹחֲטִין וְזוֹרְקִין עַל טְמֵא שֶׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 13 by choosing the other possible view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the זקני דרום hold about the פסח of a טמא שרץ owner
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסח is slaughtered and sprinkled for him
steps.whatToRemember: By the זקני דרום's view, an owner who is טמא שרץ can still have his פסח brought, but a כהן who is טמא שרץ cannot serve.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the owners' power is stronger than the priests'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש begins an attack on the זקני דרום. He asks whose power to overcome טומאה is greater, the כהנים' or the owners'. By their own view, the answer is the owners'.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: ריש לקיש blasted the Southerners. Which power is greater, the power of those who bring atonement or the power of those who receive atonement? You must say: the power of those who receive atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש starts a challenge against the זקני דרום. This line sets up his argument, which he completes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By step 14, the פסח is brought for an owner who is טמא שרץ, but by step 12, a טמא שרץ כהן cannot serve. So the owners can get past טומאה where the כהנים cannot, which means the owners' power is greater. ריש לקיש will use this in the next step to attack the ruling that a טמא מת כהן brings acceptance.

keyTerms.meaning: Blasted at them, a sharp, forceful objection
The Southerners, meaning the זקני דרום
Power, strength
Greater
You must say

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Reish Lakish blasted the Southerners:
Which power is greater:
the power of those who bring atonement, or the power of those who receive atonement?
You must say: the power of those who receive atonement;
phrases.notes: By their view, a טמא שרץ owner can still have his פסח brought, but a טמא שרץ כהן cannot serve.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא, תְּקַע לְהוּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לִדְרוֹמָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 14, together with the rule in step 12, to begin attacking the ruling in step 10 that a טמא מת כהן brings acceptance
steps.kashyaTarget: The זקני דרום's ruling (step 10) that a כהן who is טמא מת can bring acceptance for an individual's קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By their own rulings, the owners overcome טמא שרץ but the כהנים do not, so the two are not equal. The owners' power is greater, and the argument continues from there.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up ריש לקיש's full challenge. Once the owners' power is shown to be greater, he can argue that whatever the owners cannot overcome, the כהנים surely cannot.

steps.title: ריש לקיש completes his קל וחומר against the זקני דרום
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש argues: if an owner who is טמא שרץ may send his offerings and still a כהן who is טמא שרץ cannot bring acceptance, then an owner who is טמא מת may not send his offerings, so a כהן who is טמא מת surely cannot bring acceptance.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as where the owners became טמא from a שרץ, they may send their offerings, and still a כהן who became טמא from a שרץ cannot bring acceptance, then where the owners became טמא from a מת, they may not send their offerings. Isn't it logical that a כהן who became טמא from a מת cannot bring acceptance?!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש finishes the attack he started in the last step. He builds a קל וחומר to show that the זקני דרום cannot allow a כהן טמא מת to bring acceptance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 he showed that, by the זקני דרום's own rulings, the owners' power to overcome טומאה is greater than the כהנים'. With a שרץ, the stronger party (the owner) can still have his offering brought, yet the weaker party (the כהן) cannot serve. So with a מת, where even the stronger owner cannot have his offering brought, the weaker כהן certainly cannot serve.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case: if it is true there, it is surely true here
They send their offerings, meaning the offering is brought on their behalf even though they are טמא
The owners of the קרבן
Brings acceptance, meaning the כהן's service makes the קרבן valid
Isn't it logical? The standard closing words of a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. The owner and the כהן are being compared to each other. The point is not about which טומאה is heavier but that the owner is stronger than the כהן, so whatever the owner can't do, the כהן surely can't do.

phrases.english: And just as in a case where the owners became impure from a creeping animal
they may send their offerings
and yet a priest who became impure from a creeping animal cannot effect acceptance;
then in a case where the owners became impure from a corpse,
where they may not send their offerings,
a priest who became impure from a corpse,
is it not logical that he cannot effect acceptance?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the attack ריש לקיש began in step 15, using the admission that the owners are stronger.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the זקני דרום that a כהן who is טמא מת can bring acceptance
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: the owner is stronger than the כהן. With a שרץ the owner can, yet the כהן can't. With a מת the owner can't, so the כהן surely can't.

steps.title: The זקני דרום hold that even a טמא מת owner may send his offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the זקני דרום hold that an owner who is טמא מת may also send his offerings, so the starting point of the קל וחומר is wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: The זקני דרום hold: one who is טמא מת may also send his offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the זקני דרום by denying one piece of ריש לקיש's argument. They hold that a טמא מת owner can send his offerings too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר needed the fact that a טמא מת owner cannot send his offerings. If he can, there is no case where the owner fails, so nothing follows about the כהן. The argument falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold, meaning this is their opinion
The Elders of the South, the group whose view is being examined
One who became impure from a dead body

phrases.english: The Elders of the South hold:
one impure from a corpse also sends his offerings.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, "also," is the corrected wording: a טמא מת owner is just like a טמא שרץ owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 16 by rejecting its premise.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the premise of the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A טמא מת owner cannot send his offerings, so a כהן טמא מת surely can't serve.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to the זקני דרום, a טמא מת owner can send his offerings, so the קל וחומר never starts.

steps.title: Challenge from the verse of פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges from the פסוק that tells a טמא person to bring his פסח in the second month. This seems to show that a טמא מת cannot send his פסח in the first month.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: "Any man who will be טמא shall make the פסח in the second month, etc."!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 17 with a פסוק. The תורה says a טמא person brings his פסח a month later, which sounds like he cannot send it in the first month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טמא in this פסוק is understood as טמא מת. If a טמא מת could send his פסח on time, why would the תורה move him to פסח שני? So the פסוק seems to contradict the claim that a טמא מת may send his offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? The opening words of a challenge from a פסוק
The second Pesach, brought a month later by someone who couldn't bring it on time
In the second month

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"If any man shall be impure
phrases.notes: במדבר 9:10–11. The full פסוק says impure "by a dead body," which is why it's about טמא מת.

phrases.english: he shall perform the Paschal offering in the second month, etc."!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 17 from a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a טמא מת may send his offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה pushes a טמא מת to פסח שני, which implies he cannot send his פסח in the first month.

steps.title: The verse describes the preferred way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is telling the ideal way to act. If the טמא מת does send his פסח in the first month, it still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is for the מצוה, meaning the preferred way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in one word: the פסוק sets out the best way to do things. It does not say that sending in the first month fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ideally a טמא מת waits and brings פסח שני. But if he sent his offering in the first month, it is accepted after the fact. So the פסוק and the view of the זקני דרום fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: For the מצוה, meaning the preferred way to do it from the start, not a requirement that makes it fail otherwise

steps.confusionAlert: "למצוה" does not mean the פסוק is unimportant. It means the פסוק tells you what to do from the start, while sending in the first month still works after the fact.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a פסוק can describe the ideal way to act without making other ways invalid.

phrases.english: It is for the מצוה.
phrases.notes: This is the preferred way from the start. If he sent it in the first month anyway, it counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the פסוק as the preferred way, not a requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק means a טמא מת cannot send his פסח in the first month.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק gives the preferred way. Sending in the first month still counts after the fact.

steps.title: A new challenge from another verse begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new challenge, quoting the opening word of another פסוק. The rest of the challenge comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: "A man..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up another challenge against the view that a טמא מת may send his offerings. Only the first word of the פסוק appears here, and the challenge continues in what follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "והא כתיב" signal a new attack from a פסוק. We cannot see the full argument yet, so we have to wait for the rest of the quote.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? Opens another challenge from a פסוק

phrases.english: But isn't it written: "A man

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering the first פסוק, the גמרא begins a second challenge from another פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a טמא מת may send his offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet visible. The פסוק is only beginning to be quoted.
